references.text: Abimelech's earlier speech to his uncles in Shechem, which led to this conversation with the city leaders
Abimelech was the son of Gideon's concubine from Shechem, which explains the uncles' connection to the city
Laban said to Jacob, 'You are my flesh and blood' - the same expression about kinship used here regarding Abimelech
Jotham refers to Abimelech being made king because he was their brother
The tribes of Israel came to David and said, 'We are your flesh and blood' - a similar reason for choosing a leader based on kinship
David appeals to the tribe of Judah that they are his brothers and his flesh and blood - the same logic regarding loyalty through kinship
